title: Backend selection: graph.backend config + auto-detection + wire construction sites + additive manifest
description: Add an optional graph.backend config field and a resolveGraphBackend() that decides which engine to run: an explicit graph.backend value wins; otherwise auto-detect by probing each engine's version command (tokensave preferred when both succeed); when neither is installed, surface a combined install hint naming both. Wire all five construction sites (pipeline-lifecycle.ts, mcp/server.ts, cli/impact.ts, cli/graph.ts, cli/onboard.ts) to resolve the backend instead of hardcoding the tokensave backend. Evolve GraphManifest additively to record `backend` + `backendVersion` (keep tokensaveVersion; old manifests default backend='tokensave'). A CodeReviewGraphBackend stub is registered so detection can select it, but its adapters/fixtures come in Sprints 4-6.

successCriteria.description: Build + typecheck pass with zero errors.

GraphSectionSchema gains an optional `backend` enum ('tokensave' | 'code-review-graph'), default undefined (=auto-detect). A config with no backend field loads and validates exactly as before (schema back-compat).

resolveGraphBackend(config, {probe}) returns the tokensave backend when graph.backend='tokensave' or when unset and only tokensave is detected; returns the code-review-graph backend when graph.backend='code-review-graph' or when unset and only code-review-graph is detected; prefers tokensave when unset and BOTH are detected. Unit-tested with the version probe mocked (no real binaries).

When graph.backend is unset and NEITHER binary is detected, resolution fails with a combined install hint that names BOTH engines (tokensave install hint AND `pip install code-review-graph`). Unit-tested with both probes failing.

An explicit graph.backend value short-circuits detection (no probe of the other engine) and is honored even if that engine's binary is missing (the prereq check then fails with that engine's install hint, not a combined one). Unit-tested.

All five construction sites resolve the backend via resolveGraphBackend and pass it into the transport/prereq/cli/GraphClient: src/graph/pipeline-lifecycle.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, src/cli/commands/impact.ts, src/cli/commands/graph.ts, src/cli/commands/onboard.ts. With graph.backend unset + tokensave installed, every one behaves byte-identically to today.

GraphManifest adds `backend: string` and `backendVersion: string` additively; GraphArtifactStore reads legacy manifests (missing backend -> 'tokensave', backendVersion falls back to tokensaveVersion) without error. Unit-tested with an old-shape manifest fixture.
Full suite green (no NEW failures); lint clean. With graph.backend unset and tokensave present, `agent-bober onboard`/`impact`/`graph` and the run pipeline are byte-identical to before this spec.

nonGoals: Do NOT implement code-review-graph response adapters, tool catalog, or fixtures — a stub backend (id + process/prereq/cli specs only, adapters throwing GRAPH_UNAVAILABLE / marked TODO) is enough for detection to select it. Adapters land in Sprints 4-6.
Do NOT change the tokensave path behavior when backend is unset or 'tokensave'.
Do NOT add per-command --backend CLI flags (config field + auto-detect only, per the selection decision).
Do NOT remove tokensaveVersion from the manifest (kept for back-compat).
stopConditions: graph.backend config + resolveGraphBackend auto-detection wire all five construction sites; combined-hint-when-neither; tokensave path byte-identical when unset; manifest evolves additively; build/typecheck/test/lint green
definitionOfDone: An optional graph.backend enum + resolveGraphBackend (explicit-wins, else auto-detect with tokensave preference, combined install hint when neither) drives all five construction sites; the CodeReviewGraphBackend stub is registered for detection; the manifest carries additive backend/backendVersion with legacy read; the tokensave path is byte-identical when backend is unset; suite + lint green.
assumptions: Schema: src/config/schema.ts GraphSectionSchema (394-417). Add `backend: z.enum(['tokensave','code-review-graph']).optional()`. Also consider an optional `codeReviewGraphPath: z.string().optional()` mirroring tokensavePath for a custom cr-graph binary path (additive).

Detection probe = run `<binary> --version` (reuse the prereq versionArgs) and treat exit 0 + a parseable version as 'installed'. resolveGraphBackend takes an injectable probe(binary, args)->{ok, version} so tests mock it. Registry: a list of known backends [tokensaveBackend, codeReviewGraphBackend], each exposing id + processSpec.binary + prereqSpec.

Preference order when unset + both installed: tokensave first (explicit product decision). When exactly one installed: that one. When none: throw/return a structured failure whose hint concatenates both backends' installHint() for the current platform.

Construction sites all currently read cfg.tokensavePath ?? 'tokensave' (pipeline-lifecycle.ts:77,95-100,105-109; onboard.ts:70,87-92; and the impact/graph/mcp-server sites). Replace each with `const backend = await resolveGraphBackend(config, ...)` then pass backend down. The binary override becomes backend-specific (tokensavePath for tokensave, codeReviewGraphPath for cr-graph).

Manifest: src/graph/types.ts GraphManifest (13-22) + GraphArtifactStore read/write. Add backend + backendVersion; when reading a manifest lacking backend, default backend='tokensave' and backendVersion = existing tokensaveVersion. Keep tokensaveVersion written for tokensave for now.

The pipeline-lifecycle stub GraphSection object (pipeline-lifecycle.ts:230-248) already hardcodes a config; ensure it doesn't override the resolved backend — the backend is a separate injected dependency from the GraphSection config.

It only needs to be selectable + prereq-checkable this sprint.
